summary.text: Alex Bores is the Assemblymember for New York's 73rd Assembly District, which includes Murray Hill, Turtle Bay, Sutton Place, Midtown East and the Upper East Side.
His official biography says he worked as an engineer before taking office and describes legislation he passed on telemarketing fines, employee inventions, judicial seats and mopeds.

paragraphs.text: His Assembly biography says he is a fifth-generation New Yorker who was born and raised in and around the district.
It says he attended P.S. 6, Wagner and Hunter High School, graduated with honors from Cornell, and received a master's degree in computer science from Georgia Tech.

Before being elected to the Assembly, he worked as an engineer, including work that assisted the Department of Justice and two Manhattan district attorneys on violent crime cases and building software for local governments' Covid relief programs.

The biography says that in his first term he passed bills raising the maximum fine on telemarketers and protecting employees' ownership of their inventions, and that he began the process of amending a provision of the state constitution from 1846 to allow new judicial seats.

It also lists a bill that passed the Assembly asking the state to investigate the viability of personally-coded "smart guns," a requirement that mopeds be registered at the point of sale, and a bill encouraging state agencies to consider cloud computing.
Bores and his wife, Darya, live on the Upper East Side, according to the same page.
